sources.title: CM1 r22.0 Morrison microphysics, producing build
sources.reading_scope: Particle densities and inverse-slope bounds; liquid gamma shape and number concentration; mass/number exponential slopes for cloud ice, rain, snow and graupel. The repeated closure blocks around lines 1960–2055 and 5080–5260 were inspected.
sources.use: Derive volume-to-area effective radii from the saved mass and number fields, preserving the scheme's slope limits. The visible extinction uses Q_ext = 2 and the scheme's equivalent spherical particle volumes. Angular scattering uses stated HG scenarios. Ice habit and spectral particle absorption require further optical inputs.

sources.title: Physically Based Rendering, fourth edition: Phase Functions
sources.reading_scope: Henyey–Greenstein normalization, mean cosine and inverse sampling.
sources.use: Normalized HG particle phase functions with liquid g = 0.85 and frozen g = 0.8; sensitivity g = 0.7–0.9. The code uses the cosine between backward viewing and backward source directions, so its forward peak has cosine +1.

sources.title: Physically Based Rendering, fourth edition: The Equation of Transfer
sources.reading_scope: Attenuation, scattering sources and path-based evaluation of volume radiance.
sources.use: Independent spectral backward Monte Carlo with exact cell-segment optical depths, molecular/particle mixture scattering, finite-Sun next-event estimates, Lambertian ground and roulette at low path weights. Solar irradiance enters through the hash-admitted solved-column spectral product.

sources.title: Brenguier, Burnet and Geoffroy (2011): Cloud optical thickness and liquid water path
sources.reading_scope: Equations 1–5, already inspected for the preceding local cloud-column work.
sources.use: Visible area/mass relation beta = 3 rho_air q / (2 rho_particle r_effective). The new closure supplies r_effective from the saved producing-model distribution.

review_boundary: Focused equation and model-source reading. Full scholarly reading, three-dimensional cloud validation and perceptual validation remain separate evidence states.
